## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `CustomDomain`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `custom-domain`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **CustomDomain**.

## Step 2: Add a custom domain

1. <!-- manual: Sign in to [WSO2 Cloud](https://console.devant.dev). -->
2. In the top navigation, select **Organization**.
3. In the left navigation menu under **Admin**, select **Settings**. This opens the organization-level settings page.
4. Select **URL Settings** tab and then click the **Active Domains**.
5. Select **+ Add Domains**.
6. <!-- manual: In the Add a Custom Domain pane, do the following: 1. Enter your domain name. 2. Select the environment to apply the domain name. 3. Select the entity type to apply the domain name. :::tip In this context, the API entity type represents integrations exposed as APIs. ::: 4. (Optional) Select the Enable auto-apply checkbox to automatically apply this domain to all APIs in the selected environment. :::info This option is only available when the entity type is set to API. When enabled, you do not need to manually configure a custom URL for each API. The custom domain is applied automatically to all existing and new APIs in the selected environment. Only the domain is applied automatically; the original context path of each API remains unchanged. ::: -->
7. Review the generated CNAME target value displayed and create a DNS record that maps your domain name to the CNAME target value with your DNS provider. :::info When you select **Developer Portal** as the entity type, the environment is not applicable and the CNAME alias is displayed as follows: :::
8. After creating the CNAME DNS record, click **Verify**. :::info If the CNAME mapping is correct, verification completes successfully. It can take some time for the configured CNAME mapping to be globally available. :::.
9. After successful verification, click **Next**.
10. <!-- manual: Select a TLS certificate provider. You can either import your own TLS certificates or click Let's Encrypt to allow WSO2 Cloud to generate and manage certificates for you. :::note If you import your own certificate, it must meet the following requirements: TLS certificate: -->
11. <!-- manual: Issued by a certificate authority (CA), containing the domain's public key, domain name, organization details, expiration date, and the CA's digital signature. -->
12. <!-- manual: Must be an X.509 certificate in PEM format. -->
13. <!-- manual: Must be issued directly or via a wildcard entry for the custom URL. For example: -->
14. <!-- manual: Direct issuance: if the domain is apis.example.com, the certificate must include apis.example.com. -->
15. <!-- manual: Wildcard: if the CNAME is apis.example.com, the certificate can use .example.com. -->
16. <!-- manual: Must be in PEM format. -->
17. <!-- manual: Must be encrypted using RSA encryption. -->
18. <!-- manual: Must contain your domain's TLS certificate (optional if already included in the certificate) and one or more intermediate certificates in the correct order, leading back to a root certificate. -->
19. <!-- manual: All certificates in the chain must be X.509 certificates in PEM format. -->
20. <!-- manual: Root certificate: The trusted self-signed certificate issued by the CA. -->
21. <!-- manual: Intermediate certificates (if any): Certificates issued by the root CA to subordinate CAs. -->
22. <!-- manual: Leaf certificate: Your end-entity certificate issued by the CA. This may be included in the chain or provided separately. -->
23. <!-- manual: Leaf certificate: The public certificate issued by the CA (optional in the chain). -->
24. <!-- manual: Intermediate certificates: Obtain from the CA, if applicable. -->
25. <!-- manual: Root certificate: Obtain from the CA. If self-signed, it serves as the trust anchor. -->
26. <!-- manual: If the chain includes the leaf certificate: -->
27. <!-- manual: Upload the chain in the TLS Certificate field. -->
28. <!-- manual: Upload the private key in the TLS Key File field. -->
29. <!-- manual: Leave the Certificate Chain File field empty. -->
30. <!-- manual: If the chain does not include the leaf certificate: -->
31. <!-- manual: Upload the leaf certificate in the TLS Certificate field. -->
32. <!-- manual: Upload the private key in the TLS Key File field. -->
33. <!-- manual: Upload the chain in the Certificate Chain File field. -->
34. Select **Add** to save the custom domain.

## Step 3: Add a custom URL to an integration

1. <!-- manual: Sign in to [WSO2 Cloud](https://console.devant.dev). -->
2. <!-- manual: In the Integration Listing pane, click the integration for which you want to set a custom URL. -->
3. In the left navigation menu under **Admin**, select **Settings**. This opens the integration-level settings page.
4. Select **URL Settings** tab. This displays the active deployments of the integration across environments and shows whether a custom URL is configured. If a custom domain is available for an environment, the **Edit URL Mapping** icon in the corresponding **Action** column is enabled.
5. Select **Edit URL Mapping** icon in the **Action** column for the environment you want to configure. This opens the **URL Settings** dialog.
6. <!-- manual: In the URL Settings dialog, select a domain from the Domain list. :::tip -->
7. The **Domain** list shows all available domains for the integration.
8. <!-- manual: If you are configuring a custom URL for an API, specify an appropriate context path in the Path field. The field shows the default context path, which you can edit as needed. -->
9. Select **Deploy**. This creates the custom URL mapping, which appears under the **URL Settings** tab with the status **Approved**.
